A.title: FLY LOW
A.hint: Clear pictures. Planes Havana can shoot at.
A.aftermath: Navy reconnaissance squadrons in Florida are put on alert.

B.title: KEEP WATCHING
B.hint: Stay high. Stay quiet. Stay unsure.
B.aftermath: The analysts ask for more time. They always do.

D01.question: Send planes in low over Cuba?

in_1962.text: Low-level flights began on October 23, a week later than here. They brought back the clearest pictures of the crisis.

A.title: SMALL CIRCLE
A.hint: Fewer leaks. Fewer voices in the room.
A.aftermath: A dozen men start meeting in the Cabinet Room. The press is told nothing.

B.title: WIDEN THE ROOM
B.hint: More support. More people who know.
B.aftermath: Cabinet secretaries are briefed by evening. One of them talks to his wife.

in_1962.text: Kennedy kept the circle small. The ExComm met in secret for six days before the public knew anything.

A.title: CALL IT INTOLERABLE
A.hint: A public line. Hard to step back from.
A.aftermath: The press office drafts a statement. It cannot be unsaid.

B.title: SAY NOTHING YET
B.hint: Room to move. Time to lose.
B.aftermath: The schedule stays normal. Tomorrow the President campaigns in Connecticut.

D03.question: Repeat the September warning in public?

in_1962.text: Kennedy said nothing in public until October 22. He kept campaigning so the press would not notice.

A.title: SHARE THE EVIDENCE
A.hint: Allies on board. Secrets in more hands.
A.aftermath: Dean Acheson is told to pack a folder of photographs for Paris.

B.title: KEEP IT SECRET
B.hint: Full control. Allies left guessing.
B.aftermath: The allies will hear it on the radio, like everyone else.

in_1962.text: Dean Acheson flew to Paris with the photographs. De Gaulle said he did not need to see them.

A.title: QUARANTINE TO TALK
A.hint: Buy time. Leave Khrushchev a door.
A.aftermath: Stevenson is told to prepare the case for the United Nations.

B.title: QUARANTINE AND ULTIMATUM
B.hint: Set a clock. Say it out loud.
B.aftermath: A deadline is written into the draft. Someone underlines it twice.

in_1962.text: The quarantine was meant to buy time. The deadline came later, on October 27, delivered in private by Robert Kennedy.

A.title: WEAPONS ONLY
A.hint: Narrow. Defensible. Leaves them room.
A.aftermath: The proclamation lists missiles, bombers and warheads. Nothing else.

B.title: EVERYTHING, FUEL INCLUDED
B.hint: Squeezes Cuba. Looks like an act of war.
B.aftermath: Tankers bound for Havana are added to the list. Moscow notices first.

in_1962.text: The quarantine covered offensive weapons only. Adding fuel was discussed as a later step.

A.title: PULL IT IN
A.hint: More time for Moscow. Less margin for us.
A.aftermath: The Navy redraws the line. Admiral Anderson is not pleased.

B.title: KEEP IT FAR
B.hint: Safer for our ships. Faster to collide.
B.aftermath: The destroyers take their positions. The clock starts sooner.

in_1962.text: Kennedy pulled the line in after talking with the British ambassador. The Soviet missile ships had already turned back.

A.title: OPEN A BACK CHANNEL
A.hint: Say privately what you can't say publicly.
A.aftermath: Robert Kennedy calls the Soviet embassy and asks for a quiet meeting.

B.title: OFFICIAL CHANNELS ONLY
B.hint: Nothing said that can't be printed.
B.aftermath: Everything goes through State. Every word is on the record.

D13.question: Talk to Moscow off the record?

in_1962.text: Robert Kennedy and Ambassador Dobrynin became the real channel between the two governments.

A.title: AUTOMATIC RETALIATION
A.hint: Fast response. Nobody asks you first.
A.aftermath: The rule goes down the chain of command. It will not come back up.

B.title: NOTHING WITHOUT MY ORDER
B.hint: Slower. Every shot goes through you.
B.aftermath: The rule goes down the chain: no retaliation without the President.

D14.question: If a plane is shot down, who decides the answer?

in_1962.text: The ExComm agreed to retaliate if a U-2 was shot down. On October 27 one was, and Kennedy did not order the strike.

A.title: GO TO DEFCON 2
A.hint: Maximum readiness. Minimum margin.
A.aftermath: General Power announces the alert in the clear. Moscow hears every word.

B.title: HOLD AT DEFCON 3
B.hint: Serious, not maximal. Room to step back.
B.aftermath: The alert stays where it is. Some generals call that hesitation.

in_1962.text: Strategic Air Command went to DEFCON 2 on October 24, the only time in the Cold War. Its commander announced it uncoded.

A.title: PROMISE NOT TO INVADE
A.hint: Give him the way out he asked for.
A.aftermath: A reply is drafted. It says 'no invasion' in plain words.

B.title: NO GUARANTEES
B.hint: Withdrawal first. Promises never.
B.aftermath: The reply says nothing about Cuba's future. Moscow waits for a second answer.

in_1962.text: Kennedy accepted the terms of the first letter: no invasion, if the missiles left.

A.title: STAND DOWN
A.hint: Signal it's over. Trust the deal.
A.aftermath: The bombers come home. General LeMay calls it a defeat.

B.title: STAY READY
B.hint: Keep the pressure until it's done.
B.aftermath: The alert stays up. So does the tension, for weeks.

in_1962.text: The alert stayed up until November. LeMay wanted to attack anyway.

A.title: GRANT ACCESS
A.hint: For the peace, apparently.
A.aftermath: A desk is cleared in the West Wing. The Secret Service asks for it in writing.

B.title: HANG UP
B.hint: Some doors stay closed.
B.aftermath: The line goes dead. The operator writes it down anyway.

S01.question: A Soviet office in the White House?

A.title: SIGN IT
A.hint: Peace, at a very strange price.
A.aftermath: The ink dries. Somewhere, a portrait is quietly replaced.

B.title: DISSOLVE IT
B.hint: The Constitution is not negotiable.
B.aftermath: The coalition dissolves. Nobody admits having joined it.

A.title: STRIKE BEFORE THEY'RE READY
A.hint: Act while the sites are unfinished.
A.aftermath: The Joint Chiefs are told to plan for the earliest possible date.

B.title: GIVE THEM AN EXIT
B.hint: Pressure first. Force held in reserve.
B.aftermath: Nobody in the room says 'blockade' yet. Everybody is thinking it.

ROOT_1.speaker: mcnamara
ROOT_1.line: Two camps in this room, Mr. President. Hit the sites now, before they're ready, and accept we won't get all of them. Or squeeze them first and keep the planes for later. Whichever you pick, the other one stops being a plan.
ROOT_1.historical_note_es: Reemplaza D04 y D07. El ataque domino la discusion del 16 y 17/10 y la Fuerza Aerea no garantizo destruir todos los misiles (Allison, cap. 4). Kennedy eligio el 20/10; aca se adelanta.
ROOT_1.document: TACTICAL AIR COMMAND ESTIMATE: SURGICAL STRIKE EFFECTIVENESS NOT GUARANTEED.
ROOT_1.question: Strike now, or blockade first?

in_1962.text: Kennedy chose the quarantine on October 20. The air strike stayed ready, in reserve.

A.title: QUARANTINE
A.hint: Ships, a speech, and the whole world watching.
A.aftermath: Navy staff start writing the rules for stopping a Soviet ship.

B.title: TALK FIRST
B.hint: Quietly. Before anyone knows there's a crisis.
B.aftermath: The photographs go back in the drawer. On the public schedule, only Gromyko's visit.

ROOT_2.speaker: rusk
ROOT_2.line: Stevenson sent you a memo last night. Before any blockade, he says, go to Khrushchev privately and put every base on the table, Turkey included. Gromyko is here at five. The Navy says it can have a quarantine ready in four days.
ROOT_2.historical_note_es: El memo de Stevenson del 17/10 existio (Turquia incluida; el 20/10 sumo Guantanamo). Kennedy lo descarto. La cuarentena se eligio el 20/10; aca se adelanta dos dias.
ROOT_2.document: MEMORANDUM, A. E. STEVENSON TO THE PRESIDENT, 17 OCT 62.
ROOT_2.question: Blockade, or talk to Moscow first?

A.title: MISSILES ONLY
A.hint: Smaller strike. Their defenses stay up.
A.aftermath: The target list is cut to the launch sites. The Air Force says it will do its best.

B.title: THE WHOLE PACKAGE
B.hint: Airfields, SAMs, then an invasion force.
B.aftermath: Troops start moving toward Florida. The Chiefs finally look satisfied.

ATK_SCOPE.speaker: taylor
ATK_SCOPE.line: If we go, we decide now how far. Hit only the missile sites and their fighters and SAMs stay up. Take those too and we are one step from invading. The Chiefs prefer the whole package.
ATK_SCOPE.historical_note_es: Adaptada de D08. MISSILES ONLY lleva a ATK_BERLIN, THE WHOLE PACKAGE a ATK_LANDING. OPLAN 312 y 316 existieron.
ATK_SCOPE.document: JCS OPLAN 312 (AIR STRIKE) / OPLAN 316 (INVASION). COPY 4 OF 12.
ATK_SCOPE.question: How big a strike?

in_1962.text: Kennedy never ordered the strike, so this choice was never made. The Air Force had told him a strike on the missiles alone was not what it had planned.

A.title: LET BERLIN WAIT
A.hint: Keep the war in the Caribbean.
A.aftermath: West Berlin goes on rations. The allies ask who decided that.

B.title: FORCE THE CORRIDOR
B.hint: Send a convoy and see who stops it.
B.aftermath: British and French companies join the column at Helmstedt. Nobody expects them to be enough.
B.aftermath_if_failed: The column leaves Helmstedt under one flag. London and Paris were not asked.

ATK_BERLIN.speaker: rusk
ATK_BERLIN.line: Thirty hours after the strike, Soviet troops closed the autobahn to West Berlin. Checkpoint Charlie is shut. Moscow's note is one sentence long: a base for a base.
ATK_BERLIN.historical_note_es: Contrafactico. Berlin era el gran temor de Kennedy en el ExComm. LIVE OAK, el estado mayor aliado para contingencias en Berlin, existio. Jruschov no movio nada en Berlin durante la crisis. La 'falla' de la carta B no es una falla: solo cambia el aftermath si no informaste a los aliados (D06).
ATK_BERLIN.document: LIVE OAK CONTINGENCY PLANNING: BERLIN GROUND ACCESS.
ATK_BERLIN.question: Moscow closes Berlin. Force the corridor?

crisis.at_zero: No convoy is ordered. The autobahn stays closed.

A.title: GIVE HIM RELEASE
A.hint: Stop them at the border. Whatever it takes.
A.aftermath: The authority goes out by cable to Norstad's headquarters outside Paris.

B.title: NO NUCLEAR RELEASE
B.hint: Fight it with what's on the ground.
B.aftermath: Norstad acknowledges. He does not sound surprised. He does not sound relieved.

ATK_TACTICAL.speaker: nato
ATK_TACTICAL.line: SACEUR to the President. Soviet armor is moving on the autobahn in strength. If my forward units are overrun, I need release authority for tactical nuclear weapons. Now, not when it happens.
ATK_TACTICAL.historical_note_es: Contrafactico. El pedido nunca existio; el dilema si: los planes de la OTAN contaban con armas nucleares tacticas temprano y solo el presidente podia liberarlas. Norstad era el comandante supremo aliado.

crisis.at_zero: No reply. At DEFCON 2, standing procedures fill the silence.

ATK_TACTICAL.question: Give NATO nuclear release in Europe?

A.title: STOP THE BOMBING
A.hint: Take the deal before anyone counts the dead.
A.aftermath: The last sorties are recalled. The Pentagon starts counting anyway.

B.title: LAND
B.hint: Finish the job. No missiles, no Castro.
B.aftermath: The fleet leaves Florida in the dark. The beaches have code names now.

ATK_LANDING.speaker: taylor
ATK_LANDING.line: Three days of strikes, Mr. President. Through U Thant, Moscow offers to crate the missiles if the bombing stops. The Chiefs say finish it. The fleet is loaded and the beaches are marked. D-day is Monday.
ATK_LANDING.historical_note_es: Contrafactico. OPLAN 316 y la fuerza de invasion fueron reales (DEF-04). U Thant ofrecio mediar desde el 24/10.
ATK_LANDING.document: JCS OPLAN 316. LANDING ZONES, NORTH COAST. D-DAY: 29 OCT 62.
ATK_LANDING.question: Stop the bombing, or land?

A.title: PRE-AUTHORIZE
A.hint: If they fire, we fire. No delay.
A.aftermath: The authority goes down the chain of command. It will not come back up.

B.title: ONLY ON MY ORDER
B.hint: Every nuclear shot goes through you.
B.aftermath: The Chiefs take it in silence. On the beach, nobody knows what was decided.

ATK_PREAUTH.speaker: mcnamara
ATK_PREAUTH.line: First wave is ashore. Recon reports short-range rockets near the beaches, and the analysts can't rule out nuclear warheads. The Chiefs want authority to answer in kind if they're used on our troops. Without coming back to you first.
ATK_PREAUTH.historical_note_es: Contrafactico. Los Luna y sus ojivas estaban en Cuba y Washington no lo supo hasta 1992 (INT-05). El 22/10 el Presidium estuvo cerca de delegar su uso y lo prohibio sin orden de Moscu (CAL-22).
ATK_PREAUTH.document: JCS FLASH. REQUEST: PREDELEGATED RELEASE AUTHORITY, CUBA THEATER.
ATK_PREAUTH.question: Who decides if the beaches go nuclear?

crisis.at_zero: Nothing is signed. Release stays with you.

A.title: DEMAND WITHDRAWAL
A.hint: Clear. Popular. Hard to walk back.
A.aftermath: At seven, the country hears the word 'withdrawal'. So does Moscow.

B.title: DEMAND A FREEZE
B.hint: Room to bargain. Looks softer on TV.
B.aftermath: At seven, the country hears the word 'halt'. By morning, the Republicans have a better word for it.

TRK_SPEECH.speaker: rfk
TRK_SPEECH.line: Seven o'clock tonight, every network. The draft demands the missiles come out, full stop. Or you ask for a halt to the work, checked by the UN, and keep the harder words for later.
TRK_SPEECH.historical_note_es: Adaptada de D12. Discurso del 22/10 a las 19 h; el texto real exigio el retiro. Pedir solo congelar es salida temprana a E10a: en septiembre ya habia dicho que no se toleraria.
TRK_SPEECH.document: ADDRESS TO THE NATION, DRAFT NO. 6. HANDWRITTEN CORRECTIONS.
TRK_SPEECH.question: What do you demand on television?

in_1962.text: The speech of October 22 demanded that the missiles be removed.

A.title: ENFORCE THE LINE
A.hint: Stop the ships. Board if you have to.
A.aftermath: Rusk, quietly: 'We're eyeball to eyeball.' Nobody knows yet who will blink.

B.title: ACCEPT U THANT'S PAUSE
B.hint: Two weeks of quiet. For everyone.
B.aftermath: The destroyers pull back. In Cuba, the work on the sites does not stop for a single night.

TRK_SHIP.speaker: navy
TRK_SHIP.line: Soviet ships approaching the line, a submarine shadowing them. And a cable from U Thant: suspend the quarantine for two weeks, Moscow suspends its shipments, everybody talks. Destroyers request instructions.
TRK_SHIP.historical_note_es: Adaptada de C02. El pedido de U Thant del 24/10 existio (STA-09) y Kennedy no suspendio la cuarentena. Los barcos con misiles ya habian dado la vuelta el 23/10 (DEF-02).

crisis.at_zero: The Navy applies standing orders. It enforces the line.

TRK_SHIP.question: Enforce the line, or accept U Thant's pause?

A.title: SIGNAL HER UP
A.hint: Small charges. Down there, they won't sound small.
A.aftermath: After hours of it, she surfaces among the destroyers. Her crew looks like they've been in hell.
A.aftermath_if_failed: The charges fall. At that depth, nobody can tell a signal from an attack.

B.title: TRACK AND WAIT
B.hint: Stay close. Don't touch.
B.aftermath: The destroyers circle her for hours. In the end, her batteries decide for her.

TRK_SUBMARINE.speaker: navy
TRK_SUBMARINE.line: Soviet submarine near the line. She won't come up. The destroyers request permission to drop practice depth charges as a signal to surface. Moscow was told about the procedure. We don't know if she was.
TRK_SUBMARINE.historical_note_es: B-59 emergio la noche del 27/10 (DEF-06); aca se adelanta un dia. La salida nuclear existe solo con cuarentena total (D10 B) y linea lejana (D11 B).

crisis.at_zero: No order comes. The Navy follows the procedure it sent to Moscow.

TRK_SUBMARINE.question: A submarine won't surface. Signal her up?

A.title: HOLD AND VERIFY
A.hint: Find out who fired, and why.
A.aftermath: The strike is held. The pilot was Major Rudolf Anderson.
A.aftermath_if_failed: The hold order arrives late. Under the standing rule, the first aircraft have already fired.

B.title: EXECUTE RETALIATION
B.hint: Hit the site. Answer fire with fire.
B.aftermath: Four aircraft cross into Cuban airspace. In Moscow, it is already night.

TRK_U2.speaker: air_force
TRK_U2.line: A U-2 is down over Cuba. The pilot is dead. The retaliation strike on the SAM site is ready.
TRK_U2.historical_note_es: Adaptada de C03. El mayor Rudolf Anderson murio el 27/10. Kennedy no ejecuto la represalia acordada. Regla de dos rutinas, como el umbral nuclear de v0.2: con represalia automatica (D14 A) y DEFCON 2 (D15 A) a la vez, esperar falla. Con una sola, la orden de frenar llega a tiempo.

crisis.at_zero: Retaliation proceeds if it was pre-authorized. Otherwise, it waits.

TRK_U2.question: A U-2 is down. Retaliate?

in_1962.text: Kennedy held back. The retaliation agreed four days earlier was never ordered.

A.title: SEND THE ESCORT
A.hint: Bring him home. Armed as they are.
A.aftermath: The F-102s find him gliding over the Bering Sea, engine dead. He lands on the ice at Kotzebue.
A.aftermath_if_failed: The MiGs and the F-102s find each other first.

B.title: TELL MOSCOW IT'S A MISTAKE
B.hint: Explain it before they decide what it means.
B.aftermath: A message goes to Moscow through the embassy. It will take hours. The pilot glides home alone.

TRK_MAULTSBY.speaker: air_force
TRK_MAULTSBY.line: One of our U-2s on an air-sampling run near the Pole is lost. The pilot navigated by the stars and got it wrong. He's over Soviet territory, Chukotka. MiGs are up. Alaska wants to launch F-102s to bring him home. Their missiles are nuclear.
TRK_MAULTSBY.historical_note_es: Hechos confirmados (DEF-09). Los F-102 despegaron por procedimiento, sin consultar al presidente: por eso el timeout los lanza. Con DEFCON 2 (D15 A), la escolta termina en combate.

crisis.at_zero: Alaskan Air Command launches under standing orders. Nobody asked you.

TRK_MAULTSBY.question: A U-2 is lost over the USSR. Escort or explain?

A.title: MAKE THE SECRET PROMISE
A.hint: Deniable. Binding. Never public.
A.aftermath: Robert Kennedy leaves for the Justice Department. Nothing is written down.
A.locked_text: No one can carry it to Dobrynin tonight.

B.title: ACCEPT IN PUBLIC
B.hint: End it now. Pay with the alliance.
B.aftermath: In Ankara, the government asks why it heard it on the radio.

TRK_TURKEY.speaker: rfk
TRK_TURKEY.line: Jack, Radio Moscow wants the Jupiters out of Turkey, in public, and the crisis ends today. Dobrynin sees me tonight. I can give him the Jupiters in private instead, on one condition: they never say it was part of the deal.
TRK_TURKEY.historical_note_es: Une D18 y D19. La segunda carta se transmitio el 27/10 a la manana; el encuentro RFK-Dobrynin fue esa noche. Sin canal (D13 A), la promesa secreta queda bloqueada.
TRK_TURKEY.document: FBIS TRANSCRIPT: RADIO MOSCOW, 27 OCT 62, 10:00 EST.
TRK_TURKEY.question: Trade the missiles in Turkey: in secret or in public?

A.title: INSPECT AND WATCH
A.hint: Accept what can be verified.
A.aftermath: The first photographs show crates on the docks.
A.aftermath_if_failed: Moscow stalls on the details. The crates don't move.

B.title: FULL ACCESS NOW
B.hint: Everything, immediately, or nothing.
B.aftermath: Moscow accepts, grudgingly. The crates start moving.
B.aftermath_if_failed: Moscow calls the demand humiliating. The announcement is 'under review'.

TRK_VERIFY.speaker: bundy
TRK_VERIFY.line: Radio Moscow again. Khrushchev says the work will stop and the missiles will be crated and shipped home. Now we decide how we check. Surveillance and inspectors, or full access right now.
TRK_VERIFY.historical_note_es: Adaptada de D22. Sin promesa de no invasion (D17 B), Moscu se traba y cobra en Berlin (E09b). FULL ACCESS NOW mantiene las fuerzas en alerta (forces_ready), que pesa en la falsa alarma.
TRK_VERIFY.document: FBIS TRANSCRIPT: RADIO MOSCOW, 28 OCT 62, 09:00 EST.
TRK_VERIFY.question: How do we verify the withdrawal?

in_1962.text: Castro refused inspections. The withdrawal was checked from the air, crate by crate.

A.title: VERIFY FIRST
A.hint: Wait for a detonation that may never come.
A.aftermath: Nothing hits Tampa. Later, someone at Moorestown finds a test tape running in the machine.

B.title: ALERT THE BOMBERS
B.hint: If it's real, every minute counts.
B.aftermath: The bombers go to their engines. Then the news from Tampa: nothing. They stand down. Moscow saw all of it.
B.aftermath_if_failed: The alert meets a force already leaning forward. Nobody waits for Tampa.

TRK_FALSE_ALARM.speaker: norad
TRK_FALSE_ALARM.line: NORAD to the White House. The Moorestown radar reports a missile launched from Cuba. Projected impact: Tampa. Minutes, not hours. No detonation reported yet.
TRK_FALSE_ALARM.historical_note_es: Hecho confirmado: el 28/10 una cinta de prueba en Moorestown produjo la alarma (DEF-12). Lo contrafactico es que llegue al presidente.
TRK_FALSE_ALARM.question: A missile on radar. Verify or alert?

A.title: DENY IT
A.hint: No evidence of offensive weapons. Officially.
A.aftermath: The statement is read at noon. Keating says he can wait.
A.aftermath_if_failed: By evening Keating has a photograph. Someone who sat in the Cabinet Room gave it to him.

B.title: BRIEF THE LEADERS
B.hint: Tell Congress in secret. More people will know.
B.aftermath: The congressional leaders sit in the Cabinet Room. Two of them take notes.

NEG_KEATING.speaker: counsel
NEG_KEATING.line: Senator Keating is on the Senate floor again. Last week he said 'rocket bases'. Today he has locations. The press office needs a line before noon, and Gromyko is due at five.
NEG_KEATING.historical_note_es: Confirmado: Keating denuncio tropas el 31/08 y bases de 'cohetes' el 10/10. Que vuelva el 18/10 con ubicaciones es contrafactico. Kennedy reunio a los lideres del Congreso el 22/10.
NEG_KEATING.document: CONGRESSIONAL RECORD, SENATE, 10 OCT 62. REMARKS OF MR. KEATING (EXCERPT).
NEG_KEATING.question: Keating says there are missiles. What do you tell Congress?

A.title: SHOW GROMYKO THE PHOTOS
A.hint: Make Moscow answer to you, in private.
A.aftermath: Gromyko looks at the photographs for a long time. Then he asks for a telephone.

B.title: GO THROUGH HAVANA
B.hint: Talk to the island, not the empire.
B.aftermath: A message is drafted for the Brazilian ambassador in Havana.

NEG_WHO.speaker: rusk
NEG_WHO.line: Gromyko will sit in that chair at five and tell you the weapons are defensive. You can let him, or you can open the drawer. Or we leave Moscow out and go through the Brazilians. Castro is the one who has to live next to those missiles.
NEG_WHO.historical_note_es: Gromyko visito a Kennedy el 18/10 y nego todo; Kennedy no mostro las fotos (CAL-18). El canal brasileno se aprobo recien el 26/10 y nunca se uso (STA-08).
NEG_WHO.question: Talk to Moscow or to Havana?

A.title: WAIT FOR NOVEMBER
A.hint: Quiet now. Missiles later.
A.aftermath: The last week of November is cleared on the calendar. Nothing else is decided.

B.title: SET A DEADLINE
B.hint: Seven days, privately. Then you go public.
B.aftermath: Robert Kennedy delivers the deadline to Dobrynin in person. Nothing is written down.

NEG_TIME.speaker: rusk
NEG_TIME.line: Moscow's answer, through Dobrynin. Khrushchev no longer denies it. He'll discuss everything when he comes to New York for the UN, late November. Until then he asks for quiet. By late November, every site will be operational.
NEG_TIME.historical_note_es: Confirmado: el 16/10 Jruschov le confirmo a Kohler que iria a Nueva York a fines de noviembre (FRUS 1961-63, vol. V, doc. 248). Que pensara revelar ahi los misiles es interpretacion. La carta A usa trigger/else al reves: el 'exito' es la rama oculta S01; el 'else' es el final E08a, sin aftermath_if_failed para que se vea el mismo texto.
NEG_TIME.document: AMEMBASSY MOSCOW, 16 OCT 62: CHAIRMAN CONFIRMED INTENTION TO COME TO NEW YORK LATTER PART OF NOVEMBER.
NEG_TIME.question: Wait for November, or set a deadline?

A.title: ASK THEM TO HOLD
A.hint: One phone call. A promise in return.
A.aftermath: Dryfoos agrees. Reston asks for one thing in return: no blood and no war while the Times stays quiet.
A.locked_text: Too many people know. Someone else will print it.

B.title: GO PUBLIC
B.hint: Tell the country before the paper does.
B.aftermath: The networks clear seven o'clock. You tell the country there are Soviet missiles in Cuba, and that you have no answer yet.

NEG_LEAK.speaker: bundy
NEG_LEAK.line: Reston at the Times has it. Not all of it. Enough. Dryfoos, the publisher, is holding the front page for your call. If it runs tomorrow, your seven days are over, and so is everything said in private.
NEG_LEAK.historical_note_es: Confirmado: Kennedy convencio a Reston y Dryfoos de no publicar y Reston pidio la promesa de no sangre ni guerra (archivo Reston, UIUC). Fecha 21/10 segun Stern (CAL-21).
NEG_LEAK.question: The Times has the story. Hold it or go public?

A.title: ALL OF IT, MONGOOSE TOO
A.hint: Recognize him. Call off the CIA.
A.aftermath: A cable goes to Rio. Lansdale is told to stand down his teams. Nobody in Moscow is copied.

B.title: THE GUARANTEE, ON PAPER
B.hint: Promise him peace. Keep the teams running.
B.aftermath: The cable promises no invasion. In Pinar del Rio, a CIA team is still waiting for its signal.

NEG_CASTRO.speaker: rusk
NEG_CASTRO.line: Through the Brazilians, Castro answers. He will send the Soviet weapons home himself if Washington guarantees no invasion and recognizes Cuba as sovereign. And he wants the sabotage to stop. He means Mongoose.
NEG_CASTRO.historical_note_es: Adaptada de D21. Especulacion: el mensaje via Brasil se aprobo el 26/10 y nunca se entrego; Castro nunca ofrecio expulsar las armas (CIA-04, STA-08). Mongoose existio (CIA-03).
NEG_CASTRO.document: CABLE, AMEMBASSY RIO DE JANEIRO. EYES ONLY THE SECRETARY.
NEG_CASTRO.question: How much do you give Castro?

A.title: ACCEPT IN PUBLIC
A.hint: End it now. Pay with the alliance.
A.aftermath: In Ankara, the government asks why it heard it on the radio.

B.title: NO TRADE
B.hint: No deals under pressure. Nothing else ready.
B.aftermath: The refusal goes out on every network. Moscow does not answer.

NEG_OFFER.speaker: dean
NEG_OFFER.line: Radio Moscow, Mr. President, an hour ago. Khrushchev will take his missiles out of Cuba if we take ours out of Turkey. He said it in public, so whatever we answer, we answer in public too.
NEG_OFFER.question: Moscow offers Cuba for Turkey on the radio. Take it?
